title: S. Surfaces
description: `surfaces.json`: who acts on each surface of the product (caller model A). The product's shell sets the caller of every command a screen sends from the screen's surface (contract E `surface`, or its `pilot`'s when the page's URL carries `<query>=1`), replacing whatever the Micro-UI sent; a screen whose surface is not declared here, or that declares none, acts with no role and no permission (fail closed). The kits act as a surface too: the test kit's Bench and the rules' business kit as `default` unless a test names another, the journey kit checks the shell sent its screen's caller. A critical field's review role (contract I `review`, by default `role:approver`) is held by the surfaces whose gestures approve; `pilot` grants a surface from a URL query, a choice that rests on the shell serving loopback only.

default.description: The surface a test acts as when it names none: the test kit's Bench, the rules' business kit when its needs name no screen (a named screen without a surface acts with no role). Never a screen's: a screen declares its own.

surfaces.description: Every surface, by name: the caller its screens send.

by.description: The author the caller names (contract G `by`): who hears the messages.

roles.description: The roles its gestures hold: what a critical field's review needs (contract I `review`, by default `role:approver`). Empty: every command on a critical field waits for a review.

permissions.description: The permissions its gestures hold: what a DataCapability's `permissions` asks (contract F).

description.description: Who uses it, in a sentence.
